subject.title: fix(gateway): require shared secret for tailscale serve auth

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `gateway.auth.requireTailscaleSharedSecret` as the permanent opt-in contract for composing verified Tailscale identity with Gateway token/password authentication?
rationale: This introduces a new public config surface and changes a security trust boundary; code review can identify defects, but it cannot choose the supported long-term authentication policy.

options.title: Approve guarded opt-in
options.body: Adopt this setting after unsupported auth-mode combinations fail closed, generation semantics are confirmed, and exact-head behavior proof is refreshed.

options.title: Use generic auth composition
options.body: Rework the feature into a broader composable authentication policy rather than adding a Tailscale-specific boolean.

options.title: Decline the new surface
options.body: Keep the existing choice between verified Tailscale identity and shared-secret auth, relying on `allowTailscale: false`, ACLs, and documentation for hardening.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded opt-in
recommendation.body: Adopt this setting after unsupported auth-mode combinations fail closed, generation semantics are confirmed, and exact-head behavior proof is refreshed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership of the affected Gateway authentication and security-policy surface.
